newsitem.title: USA: Kmart sees holiday sales up single digits.
newsitem.headline: Kmart sees holiday sales up single digits.

text.p: Kmart Corp chairman and chief executive Floyd Hall predicted Monday that the retailer will post same-store holiday sales slightly ahead of the 1995 Christmas season.

"While our November results were a strong 4.4 percent sales increase, we are on track for low single-digit improvement over last year for the holiday season," Hall said in remarks to the Economic Club of Detroit.
Hall said Kmart expects 1997 sales to be up by that same amount over 1996.
In general, Hall said holiday sales for the entire retail industry looked to be upbeat for December.
"Clearly, the customer is spending more and is more optimistic about everything that counts than she was last year," Hall said to reporters after the meeting.

In his speech to the club, which was part of its annual economic outlook, Hall said that surveys of shoppers suggest they will spend an average of $900 on gifts in the 1996 holiday season, up from $750 last year.

He said although there are five fewer days in the traditional holiday season between Thanksgiving and Christmas this year, it does not appear that this will negatively affect total sales. He said customers have been spending more in the early days after Thanksgiving to make up for the shorter selling season.
